note: LOUD, and the record is silent on it. A celiac scanning this menu sees 'こんにゃく麺' and reads it as a naturally wheat-free option — konjac is glucomannan. It is not konjac. Staff describe it as a 冷麺-style noodle built on そば粉, and Japanese そば粉/冷麺 noodles are near-universally bound with wheat flour or wheat starch. Add an explicit warning naming this noodle; do NOT let it read as a gluten-free choice. gf_confidence stays 'no' precisely because of this.

claim: 「＜麺＞ こんにゃく麺（極細・太麺）／ちぢれ卵麺」 — a noodle sold on the menu as こんにゃく麺 (konjac noodle)
contradicted_by: Staff, quoted by two separate diners: 「こんにゃく麺はこんにゃくは入っていなくて蕎麦粉を主に使った麺との事」 (Retty, 2023) and 「こんにゃく麺はコンニャクは一切入っていなくて、そば粉を練り込んだ冷麺風の麺だそうです」 (men789 blog). It is a buckwheat/reimen-style noodle containing no konjac.
why: The menu name tells an allergy-aware visitor the noodle is konjac and therefore wheat-free, when by the shop's own staff account it is a そば粉 冷麺-type noodle — the class of noodle that in Japan almost always carries wheat flour or wheat starch as a binder.
